summary.text: A 39-year-old Caucasian woman with a normal body mass index and a past history of diffuse adenomyosis and heavy menstrual bleeding, previously treated with combined oral contraceptives, a transdermal patch and a vaginal ring, had a 19.5 mg LNG-IUS in situ since February 2024. She had two spontaneous vaginal deliveries (2015, 2019) and a maternal grandmother with ectopic pregnancy. On 8 September 2025 she presented to the emergency department with acute abdominal pain that resolved spontaneously, preceded by two days of vaginal bleeding with mastalgia and pelvic pain.

The abdomen was soft with mild tenderness. Initial transabdominal ultrasound showed normal ovaries, a right corpus luteum and a 28 mm hematic fluid collection in the rectouterine pouch. Transvaginal ultrasound in gynecology showed a correctly positioned LNG-IUS, heterogeneous myometrium consistent with diffuse adenomyosis, a 24 mm × 19 mm right adnexal hypoechoic rounded structure with the blob sign, and free hemoperitoneal fluid. Hemoglobin was 12.7 g/dL and serum β-hCG rose from 3953 to 4337 mIU/mL within 24 h.

She was admitted to the gynecology short-stay observation unit and minimally invasive surgery was recommended for suspected right tubal ectopic pregnancy. Because she requested permanent contraception, bilateral salpingectomy was planned. Laparoscopy showed a 3 cm bleeding ectopic pregnancy in the distal right fallopian tube and approximately 300 mL of hemoperitoneum with no macroscopic endometriotic lesions or nodules; right salpingectomy treated the ectopic pregnancy and left salpingectomy was for sterilization.

Histopathological examination confirmed ectopic gestation in the right fallopian tube. The surgery was uncomplicated with minimal blood loss, the postoperative course was uneventful, and the ectopic pregnancy was successfully managed by laparoscopic salpingectomy. The ectopic pregnancy occurred approximately 18 months after device insertion.
